chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from one of his companions who said:

A man had two boys in one womb, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) congratulated him, then said: 'Which of the two is the elder?' He said: 'The one who came out first.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who came out last is the elder. Do you not know that she was pregnant with that one first, and this one entered upon that one, so it was not possible for him to come out until this one came out? So the one who comes out last is the elder of the two.'
ai.seo_question: How is the elder twin determined in Islamic jurisprudence when both are born from the same pregnancy?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the principle of 'precedence of entry' (*sabaq al-dukhul*) for determining birth order, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence for inheritance and lineage. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the elder twin is the one who entered the womb first, noting that the first-born remains inside until the second-born exits, thereby resolving potential ambiguities in twin births. This ruling underscores the biological reality recognized by the Imams to ensure accurate legal attribution of seniority.
